Why do you believe that a PRO-only deck needs to be able to win using
only PRO cards? This game has many disciplines; should each of them be
able to win on their own? Of course not -- next!

Many, many winning decks use Protean in complement with another
discipline. #1 on that list is the PRO/DOM stealth/bleed deck.

So much for thinking Protean needed any help. Which reminds me, the old
weenie PRO Computer Hack decks aren't hurting all THAT much, are they?

| By the way, i hope they did something to improve a little bit Setite
| combat, in order for a
| Setite bruise and bleed deck to be able to be effectively constructed,

Have you ever tried to construct one?
Have you tried to do it the right way?

| as up to now they
| have given setites a few combat options (Skin of the Adder, Typhonic
| Beast, tongue ot
| Serpent) which imo don't worth the trouble of building a setite B&B
| (and i am not talking
| about contructing one to win a tournament, but constructing a nice
| setite B&B deck to
| have fun playing it and maybe even win a tournament with some portion
| of luck and skill)

Have you forgotten Mark of Damnation, which is an excellent card to not
only discourage your prey from blocking, but encourage him to waste
actions removing it that are NOT bleeding his prey for 6.

If he chooses not to remove it, that is just fine. A few Haven
Uncovered splashed in your deck will make him think twice about this
course of action; your grandprey might even Rush him for you, if he's a
stealthy bleeder himself.

| Finaly, about Samedi, please don't release any more stuff for this
| stupid bloodline. Don't waste your
| time and our money on developing stuff for them. Admit that Samedi was
| a mistake, forget all about
| them and move on to the other bloodlines ;)

Others have pointed out your foolishness elsewhere.

However, the inherent benchmark of any clan with OBF is:
Can it do stealth/bleed?

For today's lesson, I suggest attempting to build a stealth/bleed deck
with the Samedi. Focus on OBF/FOR, and splash THN in as necessary
(Hag's Wrinkles, etc) or appropriate. Dust to Dust is superb combat
defense for a single card; go to long, dodge, and press to end. That's
a lot of cards someone has to have to beat you, and since you have OBF,
you should be considering Swallowed by the Night to help you stay long
and avoid the Grapple.

You will require defense. Your only real option is a few Dominate skill
cards, that DOM/FOR equipment whose name escapes me, and plenty of
Deflection -- or backfilling with some Ventrue weenies and plenty of
Deflection. Votes are tricky for you, but they're tricky for many
decks; don't feel too alone.

Once you are done, you will discover that, in fact, the Samedi _can_ do
some pretty solid stealth/bleed, and therefore cannot be considered
either a "mistake", or a poor clan. Just because you're not willing to
play them in a winning manner doesn't mean they suck.

This concludes today's lesson. Thank you.

- --
Derek

Screaming Vermillian wrote:
| I think he was trying to say that Thanatosis was weak, and as a result,
| Samedhi seemed weak.

THN isn't weak, either; it's just difficult to use effectively.

Most people look at it, see a lot of combat cards, and think "hammer".
Then they go out whacking nails with THN, and realize that THN isn't a
hammer, it's an awl. No wonder the darn nails won't go in.

Then they blame the tool, not the user. People are funny.

| But what do you bleed with in an obf/for SB deck? Force of Will?
| Computer hack with laptops and retainers? Spying missions? All seems to

All of the above. The Samedi have OBF/FOR; they can take multiple
actions at stealth per turn. Three of them are inherent +bleeders,
adding even MORE help to the pile.

You only need to get up to +2 bleed on a vampire before it starts to
hurt; why do you think Pulse of the Canaille gets people Rushed so much?

I would use all the retainers, laptops, Computer Hacks, and Spying
Mission (although I would typically use Spying Mission to protect
against my big-ass bleeds getting bounced too often). That should be
more than enough to let me bleed for 3-4 with each vampire consistently,
and few decks can stand up to that for long. I would include a few
Force of Will for the surprise oust; people forget that unlike Freak
Drive, Force of Will doesn't have to be played immediately once you're
tapped. You can save it for the last action of the turn.

My own weakness is a slowish start and no inherent Deflection, but the
Ventrue weenies are probably a good call here, honestly. Saves on skill
cards, gives me spare actions if I need (but with OBF/FOR, I have lots
of actions available).

| work, but it just seems there are easier ways to do stealth bleed
| (though I guess the combat defense for provides is valuable).

And the combat defense THN provides is even more valuable.

If you are REALLY worried, include 2x Ashes to Ashes (I usually do), and
then just let that evil Donal O'Connor punch you for 6 agg from his 2nd
Tradition, instead of sneaking past him. Play Ashes, ignore it all, go
to torpor, untap, and rescue yourself with your extra 2 blood -- and
fartknocker stays tapped and just wasted a ton of his beating-cards for
nothing. ...Be sure to play the stealth on the rescue though. =)

The Samedi are suspiciously durable in combat.

| You're Mr. Super Negative aren't you? Are you a teacher IRL?

What was negative about this? I pointed out that a clan which is
commonly perceived as sucky... is actually much better than people realize.

Perhaps you didn't approve of my tone. If that's it, just spare us all;
I'm sure nobody wants to hear a rehash of "Derek said a nanny boo-boo"
again.

With regard to the "teacher" thing; what's the correlation between
negativity and teaching? This should be good =)

- --
Derek

Messages.Author: Curevei
Messages.Body:
>>Anyway, I used to clamor for a Thanatosis intercept card. Divine Sign
>lessens
>>the need for that. A prison card would make some sense, but the good ones
>are
>
>what's a 'prison card'?

Sensory Deprivation, Riddle Phantastique are good examples. Lunatic Eruption,
XTC Laced Blood would be lesser examples. Gets hard to distinguish from blood
denial when you get into The Haunting et al. Essentially, cards that lockdown
a player's ability to play the game. First Tradition is possibly less obvious
than the minionscrew but has that effect as well.

When SW came out, it seemed clear that an alternate strategy to !Malk stealth
bleed was intended in the form of !Malk prison with the likes of The Haunting,
Total Insanity, Lunatic Eruption, and the as yet unreprinted Derange (may be
other cards as well). Not to reopen the "!Malks can't do anything but stealth
bleed", it didn't seem as productive as just bleeding at stealth and, like,
putting people out of their misery quickly rather than tediously.

Prison strategies are: not as good in multiplayer because you have a much
harder time locking down more than one player; obnoxious.

While Samedi can easily get the hypothetical prison action through, if there
was a way to get rid of the irritant (take Lunatic Eruption as an example),
they'd have a hard time defending it. That limits the power. What could make
the game more interesting is the interaction involved in trying to defend
something. Sure, it's not the most difficult thing in the world to have an
interactive Samedi deck. Tournament winning Samedi with Shamblers would be one
way. For not as good decks, Samedi with Divine Sign or Samedi rush would
qualify. But, because of the not easy intercept and the easy stealth and that
you can just bleed with Samedi and oust people, it's easy to end up with a
highly noninteractive deck whatever the intent was. So, I'm trying to think of
giving them something that involves more interaction without going down the
boring "here's better combat" path. Thanatosis intercept was/is a way to
achieve that but isn't that interesting.
